claims.text: What the strip looks like A long QTc, caused mainly by a long ST segment.
claims.quote: Hypocalcaemia causes QTc prolongation primarily by prolonging the ST segment

claims.text: Aspects (abnorm in red) QT: prolonged — specifically a prolonged ST segment
claims.quote: Hypocalcemia: Prolonged QT (prolonged ST segment speciﬁcally)
The T wave is typically left unchanged

claims.text: In severe hypocalcemia (Merck): QTc and ST typically prolonged; repolarization chgs such as T-wave peaking or inversion also occur
claims.quote: Severe hypocalcemia can affect the ECG. It typically shows prolongation of the QTc and ST intervals. Changes in repolarization, such as T-wave peaking or inversion, also occur.

claims.text: Rhythm: dysrhythmias are uncommon, although A-fib has been reported
claims.quote: Dysrhythmias are uncommon, although atrial fibrillation has been reported

claims.text: Torsades may occur, but = much less common than w ↓potassium or ↓magnesium
claims.quote: Torsades de pointes may occur, but is much less common than with hypokalaemia or hypomagnesaemia

claims.text: Arrhythmia or ♡ block occasionally in severe hypocalcemia
claims.quote: ECG may show arrhythmia or heart block occasionally in patients with severe hypocalcemia.

claims.text: → (mech and diagnoses) Mech of Sx: disturbed cell membrane potential → neuromusc irritability
claims.quote: Major clinical manifestations of hypocalcemia are due to disturbances in cellular membrane potential, resulting in neuromuscular irritability.

claims.text: Eti: hypoparathyroidism, pseudohypoparathyroidism, vitD deficiency, and renal failure
claims.quote: Causes of hypocalcemia include hypoparathyroidism, pseudohypoparathyroidism, vitamin D deficiency, and renal failure.

claims.text: Also: acute pancreatitis, ↑phosphate, ↓magnesium, diuretics (furosemide), congenital disorders (ex, DiGeorge syndrome), critical illness (ex, sepsis), factitious (ex, EDTA blood tube contamination)
claims.quote: Causes of Hypocalcaemia Hypoparathyroidism Vitamin D deficiency Acute pancreatitis Hyperphosphataemia Hypomagnesaemia Diuretics (frusemide) Pseudohypoparathyroidism Congenital disorders (e.g. DiGeorge syndrome) Critical illness (e.g. sepsis) Factitious (e.g. EDTA blood tube contamination)

claims.text: ↓albumin can lower total but ⍉ionized calcium, so estimate ionized calcium from the albumin
claims.quote: However, because low plasma protein can lower total, but not ionized, serum calcium, ionized calcium should be estimated based on albumin concentration.

claims.text: Sx Mild: may be aSx or cause musc cramps
claims.quote: Mild hypocalcemia may be asymptomatic or cause muscle cramps.

claims.text: Severe (< 7 mg/dL): may cause hyperreflexia, tetany (paresthesias of the lips, tongue, fingers and ft; carpopedal and/or facial spasms; musc aches), or gen seizures
claims.quote: Severe hypocalcemia (serum calcium < 7 mg/dL [< 1.75 mmol/L]) may cause hyperreflexia, tetany (paresthesias of the lips, tongue, fingers, and feet, carpopedal and/or facial spasms, muscle aches), or generalized seizures.

claims.text: Neuromusc excitability: carpopedal spasm, tetany, Chvostek sign, Trousseau sign, seizures
claims.quote: Symptoms of Hypocalcaemia Neuromuscular excitability Carpopedal spasm Tetany Chvostek sign Trousseau sign Seizures

claims.text: Tx IV calcium gluconate for tetany; oral calcium supplements for others
claims.quote: Give IV calcium gluconate to patients with tetany; treat others with oral calcium supplements.

claims.text: Tetany: calcium gluconate 10 mL of 10% solution IV over 10 minutes; the response can be dramatic but may last only a few hrs
claims.quote: For tetany, calcium gluconate 10 mL of 10% solution IV over 10 minutes is given. Response can be dramatic but may last for only a few hours.

claims.text: Calcium infusions are hazardous w digoxin — give slowly w cont ECG monitoring, after checking for (and correcting) ↓potassium
claims.quote: Infusions of calcium are hazardous in patients receiving digoxin and should be given slowly and with continuous ECG monitoring after checking for (and correcting) hypokalemia.

claims.text: W ↓magnesium: tetany may respond briefly to calcium or potassium but = permanently relieved only by repleting magnesium
claims.quote: When hypocalcemic tetany is also associated with hypomagnesemia, it may respond transiently to calcium or potassium administration but is permanently relieved only by repletion of magnesium
